compound.name: baicalin
compound.one_liner: The main flavone of Chinese skullcap root, also abundant in American skullcap leaf; alters rosuvastatin exposure in people.

biosynthesis.pathway: flavonoid (phenylpropanoid + malonate); root-specific 4'-deoxyflavone branch in S. baicalensis
biosynthesis.note: S. baicalensis roots use a specialised FNSII-2 route to 4'-deoxyflavones [28].

occurrences.source_citation: Costine B, Zhang M, Chhajed S, Pearson B, Chen S, Nadakuduti SS (2022) Exploring native Scutellaria species provides insight into differential accumulation of flavones with medicinal properties. Sci Rep 12:13201
occurrences.note: KNApSAcK: Baicalin C00001024 in S. lateriflora. Gafner 2003 and Lin 2009 also identify baicalin as a predominant flavonoid of the aerial parts. | Basis as recorded: fresh weight (the paper's results give leaf flavone totals per g fresh weight; methods extracted ground tissue - confirm basis) | Makino 2008 (doi 10.1007/s11418-008-0230-7): flavonoids higher in S. lateriflora aerial parts than in its root. Basis (fresh vs dry weight) unconfirmed, so basis: null. Basis (fresh/dry weight) not stated by the source; excluded from /compare until confirmed.

pharmacology.mechanism: In healthy volunteers baicalin lowered rosuvastatin AUC by roughly 9-47 % depending on OATP1B1 haplotype [33].

compound.absorption_bioavailability: Poorly absorbed as such: in rats gut bacteria hydrolyse it to baicalein, which is absorbed and re-glucuronidated to baicalin; plasma exposure fell to 12 % in germ-free rats [47]. After oral baicalein in people, baicalin is the main circulating metabolite [34].

evidence.claim: Baicalin reduces plasma exposure to rosuvastatin.
evidence.test_article_detail: baicalin, repeated oral administration, randomised crossover

evidence.claim: Baicalin needs gut bacteria to be absorbed (as baicalein).

processing_stability.enzyme_dependence: gut-bacterial deglucuronidation to baicalein before absorption [47]

safety_flags.detail: Lowered rosuvastatin exposure in healthy volunteers.
safety_flags.source_citation: Fan et al. 2008, Clin Pharmacol Ther

safety_flags.detail: Four DILIN cases of liver injury with flavocoxid (baicalin + catechins from S. baicalensis and Acacia catechu); recovery after stopping.
safety_flags.source_citation: Chalasani et al. 2012, Ann Intern Med; LiverTox Skullcap

compound.teaching_note: The side-by-side number: S. lateriflora leaf 11.7 mg/g vs S. baicalensis root 26.1 mg/g in one study [24], and more in lateriflora aerial parts than its root in another [27] - not 'far lower'.
gaps: Basis of Costine 2022 values (fresh vs dry weight) unconfirmed.
Root range spans 2.6 % (Costine) to 20.6 % (Duke); basis uncertainty on the low value.
